about.tool: A broad-edged pen held at a constant 30°. Some teachers flatten the pen for the thick diagonal of z and steepen it a little for v, w, x, y; here it stays at 30°, so z's diagonal comes out thin.
about.proportions: x-height about 4 nib widths; ascenders and descenders half an x-height more (taller in Johnston's own scheme, 7 nib widths to the ascender). Capitals 1.4 x-heights, below the ascenders.
about.features: The o is a circle and the key to the hand: the arches of n, m, h and r spring from high on the stem and follow its curve; b, d, p, q and c, e share its bowl. Wedge-shaped heads added after the stem, small feet turning out to the right; a thin rising bar in e; a two-storey g; thick diagonals down to the right, thin ones from a curled head. The capitals are Roman in proportion, written with the same pen; the figures are old-style (0 1 2 at x-height, 6 8 rising, 3 4 5 7 9 hanging).
about.history: Created by Edward Johnston in the early 20th century from a 10th-century English Carolingian minuscule (the Ramsey Psalter, British Library Harley MS 2904); a teaching hand, made popular by his pupils.
